topSignals.title: Hunterbrook "Bloom's Big Lie" short report — BE plunges ~11% on Chinese scandium supply chain allegations
topSignals.text: — Hunterbrook Capital (disclosed short position in BE including derivatives) published a short report on July 8, 2026, alleging Bloom Energy's SOFC platform still depends on Chinese scandium despite public claims of supply-chain diversification. Key evidence: (a) four separate trade routes showing Chinese scandium reaching Bloom through intermediary countries, including three suppliers featured at Bloom's own May 2026 supplier conference; (b) a scalability constraint derived from Bloom's own patents: 5 GW of production would require ~220 tons/year of scandium oxide — nearly exhausting the entire projected global supply (~240 tons/year per USGS); at 25 GW (implied by the $20B backlog), ~620 tons/year would be required, roughly 10x 2025 world consumption. Bloom responded: "We are reviewing the report and will correct the record," citing "a diversified, multi-country supply chain built over two decades." BE shares fell ~11% on July 8. This is the most material fundamental challenge to Bloom's scale-up thesis published to date. Hunterbrook Media | GuruFocus | TipRanks | Benzinga | Seeking Alpha

topSignals.title: FCEL $225M offering closes today — dilution bear case crystallized; stock re-rates to ~$21
topSignals.text: — FuelCell Energy priced its upsized public offering on July 8 at $21.00/share for 10,714,286 shares ($225M gross proceeds, upsized from the initially announced $200M), with Citigroup and Barclays as joint book-runners and Goldman Sachs, RBC Capital Markets, Oppenheimer as co-leads; expected closing July 9. FCEL dragged ~14% lower and pulled BE down ~8% in sector sympathy. Combined with the 12M Fit Energy warrants at $26.44, FCEL has issued material equity in under two weeks. Proceeds fund the Torrington expansion ($200-275M, targeting 350-500 MW/year capacity). The stock re-rates to the offer price area; the remaining question is whether Torrington delivers B. Riley's positive-EBITDA target by H2 2027 as funded. GlobeNewswire (upsize) | Investing.com | StockTitan | Yahoo Finance

topSignals.title: Project Jupiter air permit in jeopardy + AEP Wyoming slips to 2030 — Jefferies Hold $246 reflects execution risk
topSignals.text: — Two major permitting and contractual risks crystallized this week for Bloom's largest backlog items: (a) Oracle's Project Jupiter (New Mexico, 2.45 GW) has no approved air permit and no completed gas pipeline; research firm SemiAnalysis revised its base-case first-power estimate from 2027 to 2029; ABQ Journal interviews with local officials and an environmental group that is suing to stop the project indicate delays into the 2030s or cancellation are possible; (b) the AEP Wyoming deal (hyperscaler co-location near Cheyenne, 1 GW committed) slid from "no later than year-end 2028" to "no later than 2030" per AEP investor slide decks. In direct response, Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith raised his BE price target from $207 to $246 (Hold — first appearance in this digest) and cited these execution risks on "a very large portion of the backlog" as the primary justification for maintaining Hold despite strong AI demand fundamentals. ABQ Journal (Project Jupiter permit) | TipRanks (Jefferies Hold) | Investing.com (Jefferies) | Fidelity (Jefferies PT)

items.text: EFCF proceedings: day 6 blackout — The 17th European SOFC & SOE Forum closed July 3 in Lucerne; six business days later no technical results from Elcogen (E3000 G2), Ceres licensees (Doosan), SolydEra, or Convion have been published online. This is now the longest post-EFCF wait observed in this digest cycle. Electronic proceedings were distributed on USB sticks to participants; company press releases remain the fastest route to usable data. Key pending items: (a) Elcogen E3000 G2 real-commercial efficiency at 650°C (stated 75% electrical / 90% CHP), (b) Doosan yield trajectory beyond Q1 2026's 80% vs. 90% target, (c) manufacturing cost per kW from ELCO I Tallinn. EFCF 2026

Hunterbrook scandium constraint: materials bottleneck for SOFC scale-up — The short report's core technical claim relies on Bloom's own patent disclosures for scandium content per cell. Scandium stabilizes the YSZ (yttria-stabilized zirconia) electrolyte in Bloom's SOFC architecture and is a key differentiator for conductivity at operating temperature. Global scandium production is constrained (primary supply is a by-product of titanium and aluminum refining; China controls ~80%+ of processing). If the supply-chain claims are validated, the materials constraint applies industry-wide — not just to Bloom — for any YSZ-based SOFC at scale. Hunterbrook Media

Project Jupiter (New Mexico, 2.45 GW) permitting timeline risk — See Top Signal #3. If the ABQ Journal reporting is accurate and no air permit is issued within 12-18 months, Project Jupiter's first-power date shifts from 2027 to 2029-2030, and the Crusoe/Cheyenne Bloom deployment (which also relies on Bloom supply) could face schedule pressure if Bloom's factory output is partially redirected. No formal delay announcement from Oracle or Bloom as of July 9; this is a risk signal, not a confirmed timeline change.

Quiet day on net-new deployment announcements. Active pipeline: Oracle/Jupiter 2.45 GW (permit risk flagged), Crusoe/Cheyenne 900 MW Phase 1, FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW (30 MW initial H2 2026), Equinix >100 MW, AEP/Bloom 1 GW (Wyoming delivery now targeting 2030), Bloom/Brookfield $25B, Nebius 328 MW EaaS.

FERC show-cause orders: July 9 intervention deadline + generation adequacy reports due July 20 — Today (July 9) is the deadline for entities to intervene in the six FERC Section 206 large-load show-cause proceedings (one per RTO/ISO, issued June 18). The RTOs/ISOs must submit Generation Adequacy Reports explaining how they intend to ensure adequate generation is available for existing and new large loads by July 20, 2026. Full tariff reform responses or show-cause justifications are due August 17. If any RTO quantifies the unmet firm-power gap from large load applications, this provides an independent estimate of the addressable market for SOFC behind-the-meter firm baseload. Stoel Rives July 8 regulatory update | FERC large-load fact sheet

ISO-NE seeking 90-day abeyance on FERC large-load order — ISO-NE and New England transmission owners announced intent to request a 90-day abeyance (filing deadline: August 3); if granted, this would delay ISO-NE's tariff reform compliance deadline to approximately November 16, 2026 and allow a stakeholder process. ISO-NE is the only RTO publicly declaring intent to request abeyance — others (SPP, MISO, PJM, ERCOT, CAISO) have not announced equivalent plans. The delay is neutral for SOFC on-site power (grid interconnection queue length is unchanged), but signals regulatory fragmentation across regions. Stoel Rives | ISO-NE / isonewswire

DOE Craig Station coal emergency order (extended through September 26) — DOE issued a 90-day extension on June 26 for Craig Station (Colorado coal plant, originally scheduled to retire) to remain available through September 26, 2026. Context for firm-power supply: winter 2026-27 grid reliability concerns in the Western Interconnection are driving emergency coal retention — reinforcing the value of on-site dispatchable power (SOFC) independent of the public grid. Stoel Rives | DOE Craig Station release
Quiet otherwise. Background: ERCOT Batch Zero self-supply pathway active (June 28); Germany EnEfG PUE ≤ 1.2 active for new DCs from July 1; EU CADA data center rating scheme delayed into Q3.

Bloom Energy (BE) — July 8: ~11% drop from Hunterbrook short report, from prior close ~$263-270 to approximately ~$235-248 range (GuruFocus cites "~11% plunge"). This follows the FCEL-contagion -8.7% on July 7 and the holiday-return bounce to ~$295 on July 6 — BE has now shed ~30% from its July 6 high in four sessions. No fundamental change to backlog ($20B), FY2026 guidance ($3.4-3.8B), or Q2 earnings date (July 28 AH, consensus ~$820M revenue / ~34% gross margin / EPS ~$0.39). Updated eight-analyst tracker: WF $217 EW | Jefferies $246 Hold (NEW — raised from $207, Hold on permitting/contract risk) | Barclays $276 EW | Roth Capital $285 Neutral | Clear Street $290 | RBC $335 OP | UBS $350 Buy | Evercore ISI $350 OP. GuruFocus short report impact | Investing.com supply chain

FuelCell Energy (FCEL) — Offering closes July 9 at $21.00/share ($225M gross). Combined dilution this month: $225M primary offering + 12M Fit Energy warrants at $26.44 ($317M if exercised). Stock trades near offer price area (~$21-22). Analyst picture: B. Riley Buy $32 | Jefferies Buy $24 | UBS Neutral $22. Torrington expansion on track financially (funded), but timeline risk remains. Q3 FY2026 earnings ~September 2026. GlobeNewswire pricing

EFCF proceedings: day 6 post-close — still unreleased — As of July 9 (six business days after the July 3 close), no stack efficiency, degradation, or manufacturing cost data from the 17th European SOFC & SOE Forum has been published by any presenting company. Watch elcogen.com, ceres.tech, solydera.com, and convion.fi press release channels. If Elcogen E3000 G2 real-commercial efficiency ≥75% electrical / ≥90% CHP at 650°C is confirmed, it would be a material LCOE model input (potential $500-1,000/kW BOP cost reduction vs. 800°C baseline). EFCF

Hunterbrook scandium analysis: first published quantification of Bloom's materials constraint — The report, based on Bloom's own patent filings and USGS supply data, represents the first externally published attempt to quantify a materials bottleneck for SOFC at scale. Key reference: global scandium production ~240 tons/year (USGS 2025); Bloom 5 GW = ~220 tons/year; 25 GW = ~620 tons/year. The report does not address whether alternative electrolyte materials (e.g., gadolinium-doped ceria, or proton-conducting electrolytes) could reduce or eliminate scandium dependence — watch for Bloom's formal response. Hunterbrook Media | StockTwits summary

Supreme Court: Trump v. Slaughter — FERC independence at risk — The US Supreme Court overturned Humphrey's Executor in a 6-3 ruling, eliminating for-cause removal protection for independent agency commissioners including FERC. Justice Sotomayor dissented that FERC is now "likely to become a purely executive agency." Near-term practical effect on SOFC: uncertain, but a less independent FERC that reverses the June 18 large-load orders in response to executive pressure would reduce interconnection queue reform speed, further strengthening the SOFC grid-bypass value proposition. Stoel Rives

lcoe.text: Scandium supply constraint: add capex sensitivity range — If Hunterbrook's findings are validated and Chinese scandium is excluded, non-Chinese scandium supply is priced at a significant premium. Recommend adding a "supply chain stress" capex scenario: +15-30% above baseline ($7,600-9,400/kW unsubsidized), reflecting the premium cost of non-Chinese or synthetic scandium. Keep the primary LCOE model at current capex. Bloom's formal rebuttal is the trigger to either drop or formalize this sensitivity.

Project Jupiter 2029 + AEP Wyoming 2030: backlog timeline risk — The two largest Bloom backlog items (~2.45 GW + 1 GW = ~3.45 GW) now have confirmed or credible delays of 1-3 years. This does not change SOFC LCOE, but means Bloom's manufacturing scale-curve inflection (and the associated capex reduction) arrives later than the H1 2027 base case. Recommend adding a "delayed ramp" capex scenario: Bloom 2 GW Fremont operational by Q2 2027 but at low utilization (large backlog items delayed); cost-curve inflection pushed to H2 2027 or H1 2028 instead.

FCEL offering at $21 closes July 9 — Market implies ~$21 fair value for MCFC expansion story. Torrington ramp (350-500 MW/year by H2 2027) is now funded. MCFC competitive pressure in the 1-50 MW data center segment arrives H2 2027 to H1 2028 most likely. Adjust competitive model: FCEL MCFC supply at scale beginning late 2027 or 2028.

FERC Generation Adequacy Reports due July 20 — If RTOs quantify the unmet firm-power capacity gap from the 438 GW+ queue backlog, this provides an independent estimate of the addressable SOFC market. Mark July 20 as a data date. FERC show-cause orders background

BE Q2 earnings July 28 (AH): primary model update trigger — Despite the short-report noise, the earnings call remains the key input event: (a) manufacturing cost per kW at 2 GW Fremont run rate, (b) product gross margin vs. ~34% guidance, (c) management response to Hunterbrook scandium claims, (d) any Project Jupiter / AEP Wyoming timeline update, (e) EaaS pricing disclosure. All five items are now material for the LCOE model.
